# 0055: Treatment is an opt-in axis layered over the fixture, and every treatment is swept beside its control

Status: accepted, 2026-10-02.
Refines:

- [0004](0004-workspace-is-a-plain-copy.md) (a workspace is a plain copy of the fixture tree) with overlays copied over the copy
- [0018](0018-fixtures-directory-and-metrics-history.md) (fixtures live under `evals/fixtures/`) with a sibling `evals/treatments/`
- [0049](0049-effort-is-the-third-matrix-axis.md) (effort is the third matrix axis) with a fourth axis that rides the same directory level

Extends [0007](0007-unpriced-model-aborts-before-spend.md)'s stop-before-spend rule to the new axis.
Additive:

- `result.json` gains `treatment`
- `history.json` gains `treatment`
- `report/index.json` gains `treatment`

Every existing capture still walks, links and replays unchanged.

## Context

A fixture is all or nothing.
It is the seed workspace a case starts from.
A case that wanted to try one change to the agent's standing instructions had to copy the whole fixture under a new name.
It then became a second case, graded and reported apart from the first.
The question a team actually asks is narrower.
Does adding this `AGENTS.md`, or this hook, change what the same cell costs and how well it does?
That is a comparison, and the matrix had no axis to make it on.

The obstacle is that neither CLI reads an instruction file the same way, and one of them reads none under the plugin's isolation.
Verified against the installed versions (claude 2.1.287, codex-cli 0.160.0), with a workspace holding a `CLAUDE.md` and an `AGENTS.md` that each named a different codeword:

- `claude --setting-sources ""`, the plugin's lever since ADR 0002, loads no `CLAUDE.md` at all, the workspace's included.
- `claude --setting-sources project` loads the workspace's, and also the user's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and every ancestor directory's.
  A workspace under a consuming repository therefore inherits that repository's instructions and its owner's.
- `claude --add-dir <workspace>` with `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` loads the workspace's `CLAUDE.md` alone, and follows its `@AGENTS.md` import.
- `codex exec` reads `AGENTS.md` from its working directory, and under a private `CODEX_HOME` reads no user-level file.

So an overlay that only drops an `AGENTS.md` into the workspace would change codex and silently change nothing on claude.
That is a full-priced run reporting a treatment it never had, which is ADR 0049's failure arriving through a different door.

## Decision

**A treatment is a named directory copied over the fixture, and it lives beside the fixtures.** `evals/treatments/<name>/` holds the files every harness gets.
`evals/treatments/<name>__<harness>/` holds files that harness also gets, copied last, so a dialect file wins at a shared path.
A portable instruction treatment is therefore an `AGENTS.md` in the first, and a one-line `CLAUDE.md` reading `@AGENTS.md` in `<name>__claude/`.
The treatments live in their own directory rather than under `evals/fixtures/` so that no treatment name can collide with a fixture name.

**The axis is opt-in, and its default is empty.** A case names its treatments with `@evalcase(treatments=[...])`, and a project may name them for every case with the `xharness_treatments` ini key.
The case wins, as it does for the matrix (ADR 0015).
Unlike the matrix there is no plugin default, because a treatment is a directory a project writes.
A case that names none sweeps exactly the cells it swept before this record.

**The untreated cell is the *control*, and it is always swept beside its treatments.** `matrix.treat` crosses every expanded cell with `(None, *treatments)`, control first.
A treatment measured alone is a number with nothing to compare it to.
So the control is not something a case can forget to ask for.
`control` is a reserved word: it names the untreated cell in `--treatment` and on the report, and no treatment directory may take it.

**A bad treatment stops collection before anything is spent.** A name must be lowercase words joined by a single `_` or `-`, so it reads like the fixture beside it.
It carries no separator that a node id, a directory level or a URL already uses.
A treatment with no directory for some harness the case is about to sweep is refused, with the case and the harness named.
Its cell on that harness would be the control under a second name.

**A treatment's files are seeded, not written.** The workspace is the fixture, then each overlay in order (ADR 0004 stays a plain copy, now of a stack).
`CaseOutput.seeded` counts every layer, so a grader asserting that no file was added does not mistake the agent's instructions for its output.

**Claude reads the workspace's own `CLAUDE.md`, and nothing above it.** The claude harness adds the workspace with `--add-dir` and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1` on every cell, treated or not.
`--setting-sources ""` stays, so the user's and the ancestors' files remain excluded.
That makes the two harnesses symmetric for the first time: codex already read its workspace's `AGENTS.md`, and claude now reads its workspace's `CLAUDE.md`.

**Treatment is a coordinate but not a level.** It rides the model's directory level after the rung, as `{model}[--{effort}][+{treatment}]`, owned by `model/layout.py` (ADR 0037).
The cell id gains the same suffix, `harness/model[/effort][+treatment]`.
A level or an id with no `+` is the control, which is what every capture written before this record holds.

**The treatment is attached by the derivation pipeline, not folded by a harness.** A session log shows what the agent read, never which overlay put it there.
`RunResult.treatment` is set by `runtime/pipeline.py` from the cell, and carried forward from the stored result on a replay, exactly as `effort` is (ADR 0049).

## Consequences

Three emitted documents gain one key each: `result.json`, `history.json` and `report/index.json` all carry `treatment` (null or empty for the control).
It is mirrored in `report-ui/src/lib/types.ts` and the shipped glossary.
The characterization goldens move by that key alone, `"treatment": null`, and no measured value in them changes.
That is the evidence that this adds a coordinate rather than redistributing one.

The report groups a control and its treated twin as two rows of the same case and model.
The comparison the axis exists for is then one glance.
`--treatment` narrows a sweep the way `--effort` does, and `--treatment control` selects the untreated arm alone.

Two cells of one case may now differ in nothing but their treatment, so the build workspace name includes it.

The claude lever changes the control arm in one case: a fixture that already shipped a `CLAUDE.md` is now read, where before it was ignored.
That is a correction rather than a regression.
A user running claude in that repository would have read it, and codex always did.

Hooks are not given a lever here.
A treatment may carry a `.claude/settings.json`, but `--setting-sources ""` still excludes it.
Admitting it is a separate decision with its own contamination question, and this record does not make it.

## Lens

A change to an agent's instructions is only measured when the same cell runs without it.
So the untreated cell is never optional: it is swept every time a treatment is.
A treatment that copies nothing onto some harness is that harness's control billed twice under a second name.
So the overlay must exist for every harness it is swept on, and collection refuses it otherwise.
An overlay the CLI never reads is the same failure arriving later.
So the lever that makes a harness read it is verified before it is trusted.
